batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 distinct supplied candidates and their supplied point predictions before measurement. Prioritize crossed loading comparisons, unresolved solvent-response shapes and connected structural experiments, with exploration directed toward transferable relationships across ester, ether, nitrogen-containing and aromatic-carbonyl rows.

choices.reason: 2,6-Dimethoxybenzaldehyde, 2/1, 100 uL sample in 500 uL DCM. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 20.577983856201172/42.75478744506836 mL. Measures one missing factorial corner separating sample volume from DCM volume after the two measured diagonal conditions differed by 40.23 mL in completion.

2,6-Dimethoxybenzaldehyde, 2/1, 150 uL sample in 300 uL DCM. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 20.569570541381836/42.75129318237305 mL. Completes the crossed loading design. The nearly identical predictions for its two missing corners leave sample-volume, DCM-volume and interaction explanations unresolved.

Para-methoxybenzaldehyde, 50/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 40.407249450683594/70.6191177368164 mL. Loading matches measured 20/1 and 10/1 conditions. Tests weak-eluent extrapolation after both new 20/1 labels were historically underestimated but showed similar completion across sample loads.

Dimethoxy-methylbenzene, 20/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 19.592287063598633/36.381858825683594 mL. Locates the rise toward measured 50/1 endpoints of 31.82/55.57 mL. The selected trimethoxybenzene comparison tests whether its large recent correction transfers correctly into interpolation.

Trimethoxybenzene, 20/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 13.586956024169922/19.564870834350586 mL. Loading matches its measured 50/1 anchor. Alongside dimethoxy-methylbenzene at the same composition and solvent setup, tests the predicted intermediate structural contrast; densities differ.

Para-dimethoxybenzene, 50/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 17.04566764831543/26.67011260986328 mL. Adds a common-composition reference to the measured substituted ethers. Its 400 uL DCM volume differs from their 300 uL, so this tests conditional structural transfer rather than isolating ether count.

Methoxyethyl acetoacetate, pure EA, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 5.288253307342529/8.08759880065918 mL. Loading matches its measured 1/1 endpoints of 10.82/27.16 mL. Tests the predicted sharp final contraction after completion remained historically underestimated at 1/1.

Methoxyethyl acrylate, 5/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 18.217073440551758/36.80018615722656 mL. Predicted completion exceeds its measured 10/1 completion of 34.90 mL while onset contracts. Tests an unconfirmed endpoint-specific response and transfer from the more retained ether-containing ketoester; the measured anchor used 50 uL.

Para-aminobenzonitrile, 2/1, 50 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 15.288311958312988/33.92457580566406 mL. Loading matches its measured 1/1 anchor and selected 5/1 experiment. Measuring both directly tests the predicted 2/1-later-than-5/1 response.

Para-aminobenzonitrile, 5/1, 50 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 9.690484046936035/28.369688034057617 mL. Paired with the loading-matched 2/1 point, distinguishes a real response inversion from interpolation failure. The selected meta isomer supplies a positional comparison at identical solvent and sample-volume settings.

Meta-aminobenzonitrile, 5/1, 50 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 8.372466087341309/25.642786026000977 mL. Loading matches its measured 2/1 endpoints of 14.22/31.49 mL. Tests the same predicted response inversion in a positional isomer and provides a controlled comparison with para-aminobenzonitrile.

2,6-Lutidine, 5/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 15.684542655944824/39.489532470703125 mL. Resolves the intermediate response after the weak-eluent label exposed a 22.74 mL historical completion underestimate. Its measured 2/1 and 10/1 anchors used 150 uL, retained as a covariate.

Diethylaminoethyl acrylate, 1/1, 150 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 7.70811653137207/16.55324935913086 mL. Tests the predicted contraction from the measured 2/1 endpoints of 16.43/32.81 mL for an aliphatic tertiary amine with an ester. That anchor used 100 uL, so sample loading remains a covariate.

Quinoline, 5/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 29.12233543395996/53.092384338378906 mL. Loading matches its measured 2/1 and 10/1 anchors. Tests interpolation and transfer from the now better constrained methylquinoline curve without assuming identical retention scales.

Para-nitrobenzaldehyde, 1/1, 150 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 5.26570463180542/20.202930450439453 mL. Tests the predicted completion rebound relative to measured 2/1 endpoints of 5.52/16.05 mL and provides an independent scaffold check for nitrobenzophenone. The measured 2/1 anchor used 100 uL, limiting causal interpretation.

Para-nitrobenzophenone, 1/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 7.9674530029296875/29.91801643371582 mL. The selected loading-matched 2/1 point has earlier predicted endpoints. Tests whether this unusual strong-eluent response is supported, rather than extrapolating from the differently loaded measured 5/1 record.

Para-nitrobenzophenone, 2/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 6.533385753631592/21.653900146484375 mL. Completes the controlled 2/1-to-1/1 comparison. Both endpoints distinguish a completion-dominated rebound from a general retention-scale error and constrain transfer across nitro aromatic carbonyls.

First ethyl 2-bromopropionate label, 20/1, 50 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 11.04977035522461/19.051870346069336 mL. Paired with ethyl 2-bromoisobutyrate under the same solvent setup, tests alpha-substitution effects within bromoesters. Densities and therefore loading amounts differ.

Ethyl 2-bromoisobutyrate, 20/1, 50 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 8.13528060913086/12.97033977508545 mL. Loading matches its measured 10/1 anchor. Supplies the condition reference for interpreting the new less-substituted bromoester and tests the predicted lower retention associated with its changed alpha-carbon environment.

First ethyl para-chlorobenzoate label, 40/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 9.581206321716309/19.648468017578125 mL. Tests methyl-to-ethyl benzoate transfer using measured methyl-analogue and related ester records. Adds connected exploration across a substantial ester neighborhood without presuming a large error from novelty.

First 2,4-dimethylbenzaldehyde label, 20/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 9.588032722473145/22.122539520263672 mL. Together with its selected 50/1 point and the ortho-tolualdehyde pair, tests predicted weak-eluent response differences among simple aromatic aldehydes. Steric effects are a prior, not an established finding here.

First ortho-tolualdehyde label, 20/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 6.714295864105225/17.24427604675293 mL. Starts a loading-matched two-composition curve alongside 2,4-dimethylbenzaldehyde. Tests structural transfer without propagating methoxybenzaldehyde corrections as a common aromatic-carbonyl offset.

First aryl/benzylic dibromide methoxybenzene label, 50/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 7.855511665344238/16.867568969726562 mL. Tests weak-eluent transfer within halogenated ethers after a major failure for another substituted ether. Its 600 uL DCM volume remains a covariate; the related failure does not establish an error here.

First bromo-iodo trifluoromethoxybenzene label, 50/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 7.857473373413086/17.782896041870117 mL. Tests transfer from measured trifluoromethoxy aryl iodide and early halogenated references. Adds a fluorinated-ether environment that can constrain excessive corrections learned from polyethers.

Ortho-tolualdehyde, 50/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 9.004105567932129/21.467912673950195 mL. Completes its controlled 20/1-to-50/1 curve. The predicted rise is modest compared with selected 2,4-dimethylbenzaldehyde, testing structural response-shape transfer beyond a single new-molecule condition.

Benzosuberone, 10/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 5.368784427642822/16.302289962768555 mL. Loading matches its measured 20/1 anchor, whose onset was historically overpredicted by 11.07 mL while completion was much closer. Tests whether its relatively early onset persists across composition.

Methyl-substituted tetralone, 20/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 5.785758018493652/16.43951988220215 mL. Loading matches its measured 5/1 anchor. Tetralone at the same composition measured 13.52/30.38 mL. Tests the predicted large substitution effect, retaining density differences.

1-Phenylpropan-1-ol, 10/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 12.403962135314941/29.754743576049805 mL. Loading matches its measured 20/1 endpoints of 34.61/59.42 mL. Tests the predicted steep contraction and transfer between secondary benzylic alcohols after related onset records showed heterogeneous behavior.

Para-methoxyphenethyl alcohol, pure EA, 50 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 3.9404067993164062/9.079052925109863 mL. Loading matches its accurately predicted acquired 2/1 point. Tests whether the strong-eluent contraction observed for naphthyl alcohols extends to this ether-containing primary alcohol; its measured 1/1 anchor used 100 uL.

Meta-bromobenzyl alcohol, 5/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 20.01980209350586/33.4744987487793 mL. Exactly matches loading of its measured 10/1 and 2/1 anchors. Locates the response after weak-eluent completion remained historically underestimated, testing transfer from other primary alcohol environments.

1-Phenylcyclohexanol, 20/1, 50 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 25.87027359008789/53.9190559387207 mL. Tests the predicted weak-eluent rise for a constrained tertiary donor environment against its measured 5/1 endpoints of 9.52/14.71 mL. That anchor used 150 uL, so loading remains a covariate.

2,4-Dimethylbenzaldehyde, 50/1, 100 uL. Frozen V1/V2 prediction: 15.456478118896484/32.98125457763672 mL. Completes its loading-matched curve and common-composition comparison with ortho-tolualdehyde. Tests whether additional methyl substitution changes weak-eluent slope and endpoint spacing as predicted.

hypotheses.content: Aromatic-carbonyl retention depends on structural environment in an endpoint-specific way. The measured fused-ring comparison differs more strongly in onset than a common offset would imply. Methyl substitution and steric environment are plausible extensions to test, not established explanations for the new aldehydes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected ring-size, substitution and composition comparisons can improve transfer across carbonyl rows while preventing corrections for one retained scaffold from spreading to early-eluting analogues.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does benzosuberone retain its early onset at 10/1, is methyl-substituted tetralone much earlier than tetralone at 20/1, and do the new aldehydes have different weak-eluent slopes?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen environments require distinct solvent-response curves and separate onset/completion learning. Recent lutidine, dibenzylamine and methylquinoline outcomes support this distinction. The predicted aminobenzonitrile 2/1-later-than-5/1 response remains untested and may be an interpolation failure.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The batch tests response direction in positional isomers and interpolation across nitrogen environments without relying on a shared nitrogen or presumed-basicity correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the aminonitrile inversions real, and do intermediate lutidine, quinoline and tertiary-amino acrylate labels support their current scaffold-specific curves?

hypotheses.content: Alcohol response depends on donor environment and composition. The predicted naphthylethanol strong-eluent onset reversal was rejected: pure EA eluted much earlier than 1/1. Strong boundary contraction is supported for the measured naphthyl alcohols, while transfer across other alcohol environments remains heterogeneous.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Boundary and intermediate labels can teach where contractions occur and how they transfer between benzylic, remote primary, secondary and constrained tertiary donor environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does methoxyphenethyl alcohol contract similarly in pure EA, and are the predicted response scales correct for bromobenzyl, secondary benzylic and cyclic tertiary alcohols?

hypotheses.content: Ester response cannot be inferred from acceptor count or a common long-retention correction. Recent ketoester outcomes differ in scale and endpoint behavior. Ether functionality, carbonyl arrangement and alpha substitution are plausible determinants whose transfer needs direct testing.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A boundary test, an ether-acrylate interpolation test and connected bromoester/benzoate exploration constrain common ester neighborhoods without assigning an unsupported adsorption or tautomeric mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does methoxyethyl acetoacetate approach the predicted pure-EA endpoints, does methoxyethyl acrylate show the predicted completion rebound, and does alpha substitution transfer correctly in bromoesters?

hypotheses.content: Weak-eluent aromatic-ether response is substitution-dependent. The earlier expectation that trimethoxybenzene would be later than dimethoxy-methylbenzene at 50/1 was contradicted: measured endpoints were 22.94/36.12 and 31.82/55.57 mL, respectively. These conditional comparisons do not establish ether count as the cause.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Intermediate measurements test whether retraining learned a transferable structure-by-composition interaction. Related halogenated and fluorinated ethers test the correction's limits in earlier-retaining regions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do the two ether curves diverge between 5/1 and 50/1, and do para-dimethoxybenzene and the new halogenated ethers follow their predicted weak-eluent scales?

hypotheses.content: The methoxy-aromatic records do not support one smooth universal loading response. At 2/1, the dimethoxybenzaldehyde discrepancy changes both sample and DCM volume. At 20/1, para-methoxybenzaldehyde shows a moderate onset difference but similar completion across 50 and 100 uL. Loading interactions and unrecorded run variation remain competing explanations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Completing the missing factorial corners can reveal whether recorded loading features explain the discrepancy and limit unsupported propagation of a loading effect to other rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the missing 2/1 corners track sample volume, DCM volume, an interaction or neither, and does para-methoxybenzaldehyde's measured 20/1 scale extrapolate correctly to 50/1?

hypotheses.content: The predicted 1/1 completion rebound for nitro aromatic carbonyls is unresolved. A related methyl benzoylformate comparison has a measured completion rebound but also changes sample volume, so it cannot validate the nitro predictions. Matched measurements are needed before classifying these curves as real behavior or model failure.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The matched ketone pair and independent aldehyde check distinguish an endpoint-specific response from transfer artifacts without imposing monotonicity unsupported by the catalog.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does nitrobenzophenone complete later at 1/1 than 2/1 under identical loading, and does nitrobenzaldehyde show the same direction after accounting for its sample-volume difference?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes changed the priorities. Naphthylethanol measured 6.01/10.57 mL in pure EA versus 18.27/33.28 at 1/1, rejecting the predicted onset reversal; naphthylmethanol also contracted strongly in pure EA. Pyridyl propiophenone nevertheless completed at 21.09 mL in pure EA against a 7.43 mL acquisition prediction, so a universal strong-eluent collapse is unsupported. Dimethoxy-methylbenzene at 50/1 measured 31.82/55.57 against 7.65/13.53 predicted, while trimethoxybenzene and anisole were much closer. This shifts attention toward intermediate ether response and structural transfer. The new dimethoxybenzaldehyde 2/1 point was much earlier than the older differently loaded record, making the missing factorial corners particularly informative. Both para-methoxybenzaldehyde 20/1 labels were historically underestimated, but their completions differed by only 1.57 mL, weakening a large general completion-versus-load explanation. Methylquinoline interpolation was comparatively close, dibenzylamine was earlier than predicted, and lutidine completion remained underestimated. Methoxyethyl acetoacetate retained a completion underestimate at 1/1, whereas tert-butyl acetoacetate at 20/1 was earlier than predicted. Fused-ring ketone outcomes exposed greater onset than completion errors. Cinnamic acid's 5/1 completions were similar across DCM volumes, weakening a composition-independent loading-solvent-volume offset; its cause remains unresolved. Several new halogenated compounds were comparatively accurate, reducing the case for isolated novelty-only probes. All errors discussed are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines hypothesis discrimination with connected exploration. The dimethoxybenzaldehyde factorial corners address confounded loading evidence. Paired ether intermediates, two new aldehyde response curves, aminonitrile comparisons and the nitrobenzophenone pair constrain response direction and shape. Alcohol, lutidine, quinoline and ester measurements target unresolved transitions or boundaries after feedback showed heterogeneous correction transfer. Fused ketones test whether structural effects on onset and completion remain distinct. New bromoesters, a benzoate and halogenated ethers extend coverage within common chemical neighborhoods and can protect earlier-retaining rows from excessive corrections learned from polar compounds. No identical experiment tuple is selected twice. All 32 supplied IDs and point predictions are frozen in the choices. Density, sample volume, loading solvent and its volume remain covariates wherever comparisons are unmatched; density times sample volume is the loading feature, not an independent label. The objective is improved overall Row V1/V2 accuracy after retraining. Elution interval width is an outcome, and single-predictor quantile widths are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty.
